content.text: Looking at this diff, all three changes are purely presentational CSS class additions for animations (transition-modal, animate-fade-in-fast, animate-fade-in-up, animate-dropdown-in). No data flow, no sinks, no auth logic, no new inputs. Let me verify by reading the touched regions.

All three changes are purely presentational — adding CSS animation classes (`transition-modal`, `animate-fade-in-fast`, `animate-fade-in-up`, `animate-dropdown-in`) and a wrapping `<div>` around already-rendered React children. No new inputs, no new sinks, no auth/authz logic, no data flow, no template interpolation, no attacker-controlled values touched. The wrapping div around the CalendarDatePicker and around the `<>` fragment (viewMore branch) does not change conditional rendering or data passed.

No security-relevant behavior is introduced.
